questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless ulcer on the right hand with a central black eschar, surrounded by extensive non-pitting oedema. There is no fever. Gram stain of the ulcer exudate shows large gram-positive rods. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax caused by Bacillus anthracis classically presents as a painless papule evolving into a black eschar (malignant pustule) with surrounding gelatinous, non-pitting oedema. Gram stain shows large gram-positive rods in bamboo-rod arrangement.

questions.q: A 28-year-old sexually active male presents with painless, indurated, clean-based genital ulcer with bilateral non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy (rubbery nodes). Dark field microscopy of the ulcer exudate shows spiral organisms. Which syphilis stage is this?
questions.exp: Chancre of primary syphilis is a single, painless, indurated, clean-based ulcer with regional non-tender lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy demonstrates Treponema pallidum spirochetes. Secondary syphilis appears 6–8 weeks later with systemic features.

questions.q: A 45-year-old leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden onset reddening and tenderness of pre-existing skin lesions with fever and malaise. Nerve function remains intact. What is this reaction called?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 reaction) occurs in lepromatous/borderline lepromatous leprosy. It is an immune complex (Type III hypersensitivity) mediated reaction presenting as tender erythematous nodules with systemic features. Type 1 (reversal) reaction involves nerve function deterioration.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman develops tense, fluid-filled blisters on normal-appearing skin and erythematous plaques. Nikolsky sign is negative. Biopsy shows sub-epidermal blister with eosinophilic infiltrate and DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense blisters on normal or urticarial skin; Nikolsky sign is negative. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ (hemidesmosomes, BP180/BP230 antigens). Sub-epidermal split histologically with eosinophils distinguishes it from pemphigus.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with pearly, translucent papule with rolled edges and telangiectasias on the nose, with central ulceration. Which histological finding is most characteristic?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) classically shows islands of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artefact (separation from stroma). It is the most common skin malignancy, arising from basal cells of epidermis/hair follicles.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with multiple, violaceous, non-tender nodules on the skin and palate. Biopsy shows spindle cells forming vascular slits with extravasated RBCs. HHV-8 is positive. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma associated with HIV is caused by HHV-8. Histology shows spindle cell proliferation with vascular slit formation and extravasated RBCs. Bacillary angiomatosis (Bartonella) may mimic KS clinically but lacks HHV-8 and shows neutrophilic infiltrate.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive (1:320, homogeneous pattern). Anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm antibodies are positive. Which skin biopsy finding using DIF of non-lesional sun-protected skin is most specific for her diagnosis?
questions.exp: The lupus band test (LBT) shows granular deposits of IgG, IgM, and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction on DIF of non-lesional, sun-protected skin in SLE. Positive LBT in non-lesional skin is specific for systemic (not discoid) lupus.

questions.q: A patient on long-term griseofulvin develops phototoxicity and porphyria-like symptoms. Griseofulvin exerts its antifungal action by which mechanism?
opts: Inhibiting ergosterol synthesis by blocking 14-alpha demethylase
Disrupting microtubule assembly and inhibiting fungal mitosis
Forming pores in the fungal cell membrane
Inhibiting beta-glucan synthesis in the cell wall
questions.exp: Griseofulvin binds to tubulin and inhibits microtubule polymerization, arresting fungal cell mitosis at metaphase. It is fungistatic and used for dermatophytosis. It is a CYP inducer and can precipitate porphyria.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child presents with honey-crusted erosions around the nose and mouth. Culture grows Staphylococcus aureus producing exfoliative toxin A. Which protein does this toxin target?
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome and bullous impetigo are caused by exfoliative toxins A and B (ET-A, ET-B), which cleave Desmoglein 1 (Dsg1) — the desmosomal cadherin predominant in the superficial epidermis — leading to intra-epidermal splitting at the granular layer.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with well-defined, scaly, salmon-pink plaques on the elbows and knees with nail pitting, onycholysis, and 'oil drop' discolouration. Koebner phenomenon is positive. The Auspitz sign is due to?
opts: Thinning of the suprapapillary plate with dilated capillary loops
questions.exp: Auspitz sign (bleeding points on removal of scale in psoriasis) results from thinning of the suprapapillary plate and elongated dermal papillae with dilated, tortuous capillaries that are easily disrupted.

questions.q: A newborn presents with widespread blistering from birth. Biopsy shows blisters at the level of the lamina lucida. Electron microscopy shows reduced/absent hemidesmosomal plaques. The defect is in which protein?
questions.exp: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (JEB) Herlitz type has blistering at the lamina lucida with reduced/absent hemidesmosomes. It is caused by mutations in integrin alpha-6-beta-4, collagen XVII (BP180), or laminin-332. Collagen VII mutations cause dystrophic EB; keratin 5/14 cause simplex EB.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with a single hypopigmented, anaesthetic patch on the left forearm. Slit-skin smear is negative. Biopsy shows epithelioid cell granulomas with lymphocytic cuffing but no AFB. Nerve involvement is present. Lepromin test (Mitsuda) is strongly positive. Classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) shows 1-2 well-defined, anaesthetic hypopigmented patches, negative SSS, strongly positive Mitsuda reaction (cell-mediated immunity intact), and biopsy with well-formed epithelioid granulomas with lymphocytic cuffing, few or no AFB.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with intensely pruritic papules and burrows in the interdigital spaces, wrists, and genitalia. Other family members are similarly affected. Which finding on dermoscopy is pathognomonic?
opts: Delta-wing jet sign (triangular brown structure with white tail)
questions.exp: Dermoscopy of scabies shows the 'jet with contrail' or delta-wing jet sign: a triangular/V-shaped brown structure (mite body) at the end of a whitish serpiginous burrow. This is pathognomonic for Sarcoptes scabiei infestation.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops firm, non-pitting oedema of the hands and face, Raynaud's phenomenon, and telangiectasias. Pulmonary hypertension is noted on echo. Anti-centromere antibody is positive. Which clinical subset does she have?
opts: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc) — CREST syndrome
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) is limited cutaneous SSc. Anti-centromere antibodies (ACA) are characteristic. Pulmonary hypertension is the main cause of death. dcSSc is associated with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I).

questions.q: A 50-year-old immunocompromised patient presents with painful grouped vesicles in a dermatomal distribution on the left thorax, crossing the midline slightly. Two days later, the patient develops ipsilateral facial palsy, loss of taste on anterior 2/3 tongue, and vesicles in the external auditory meatus. Which syndrome?
questions.exp: Ramsay Hunt syndrome (herpes zoster oticus) is due to VZV reactivation in the geniculate ganglion of cranial nerve VII (facial nerve). It presents with ear pain, vesicles in the external auditory meatus, ipsilateral facial palsy, and loss of taste in anterior 2/3 of tongue.

questions.q: A 35-year-old is undergoing patch testing for suspected contact dermatitis. The reading at 48 hours shows erythema with papules and vesicles, and the same morphology is present at 96 hours (D4) with slight increase. How is this graded?
questions.exp: ICDRG grading: + = erythema with papules; ++ = erythema, papules, vesicles (strong positive); +++ = bullous or ulcerative reaction (extreme positive). Persistence or increase at D4 confirms allergic contact dermatitis. Irritant reactions typically peak at D2 and fade by D4.

questions.q: A patient receives intralesional triamcinolone for a keloid. Which mechanism accounts for its efficacy in this context?
opts: Inhibition of fibroblast proliferation and reduced collagen synthesis
Activation of collagenase to degrade existing collagen
Increase in TGF-beta expression promoting collagen remodelling
Direct keratinocyte apoptosis reducing scar bulk
questions.exp: Intralesional corticosteroids (triamcinolone acetonide) reduce keloid/hypertrophic scar by inhibiting fibroblast proliferation, decreasing collagen synthesis, and increasing collagenase production. They also reduce the inflammatory infiltrate which drives fibroblast activity.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with hyperpigmented macules on the cheeks and forehead, worse in summer, first appearing during pregnancy. Wood's lamp examination shows marked accentuation of the pigment. What layer is primarily affected?
questions.exp: Wood's lamp accentuates epidermal (superficial) pigment and does not enhance dermal pigment. Accentuation confirms predominantly epidermal melasma, which responds better to treatment. Mixed-type shows partial enhancement; dermal type shows no enhancement.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male farmer has multiple actinic keratoses on the scalp. Biopsy of one lesion shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia. The treatment of choice to prevent progression to invasive SCC is?
questions.exp: Topical 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) is a first-line field therapy for multiple actinic keratoses, inhibiting thymidylate synthase to block DNA synthesis in rapidly proliferating dysplastic cells. Photodynamic therapy and imiquimod are alternatives. Mohs surgery is for established invasive SCC.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with diffuse non-scarring hair loss. Hair pull test reveals telogen hairs predominantly. She had an episode of high fever with typhoid 3 months ago. Which type of hair loss is this?
questions.exp: Telogen effluvium is diffuse non-scarring hair loss caused by premature conversion of anagen to telogen hairs following a physiological stressor (fever, surgery, childbirth, crash dieting). It occurs 2–4 months after the trigger. Hair pull test shows >25% telogen hairs (club hairs).

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with whitish plaques in the mouth that cannot be wiped off. KOH preparation shows pseudohyphae and blastospores. Oral nystatin fails. He is tested and found to be HIV positive with CD4 count 80/µL. Most appropriate systemic treatment?
questions.exp: Oropharyngeal candidiasis in HIV/AIDS is treated with systemic azoles when topical therapy fails. Fluconazole is the drug of choice — it is well absorbed orally, with excellent bioavailability, minimal drug interactions compared to itraconazole, and candidal coverage. Griseofulvin and terbinafine are ineffective against Candida.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with painless, firm, non-tender ulcer on the penis with a smooth, indurated base. Inguinal nodes are bilateral, non-tender, rubbery. RPR titre is 1:64. Partner was recently treated for syphilis. VDRL with prozone phenomenon means?
opts: False negative due to antigen excess
False positive due to non-specific antibody
False negative due to antibody excess
questions.exp: The prozone phenomenon in syphilis serology occurs when excess antibody (in high-titre secondary syphilis) saturates all antigen sites, preventing cross-linking and visible agglutination, giving a false-negative result. Diluting the serum restores reactivity. Antigen excess causes post-zone phenomenon.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman has recurrent blisters in the oral cavity and skin for the last 2 years. Nikolsky sign is positive. Biopsy shows supra-basal acantholysis with 'tombstone' pattern of basal cells. DIF shows intercellular IgG and C3 throughout the epidermis ('chicken-wire' pattern). Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris: flaccid blisters with positive Nikolsky sign, supra-basal acantholysis (tombstone appearance), DIF shows intercellular IgG/C3 in a chicken-wire pattern. Autoantibodies target Dsg3 (mucosal) and Dsg1 (cutaneous). Pemphigus foliaceus targets only Dsg1 and spares mucosae.

questions.q: A 17-year-old presents with comedones, papules, pustules, and nodulocystic lesions on the face and back. He has significant post-acne scarring. Oral isotretinoin is started. Which monitoring parameter is mandatory before and during therapy?
opts: Serum uric acid and CBC monthly
Fasting lipid profile and liver function tests
Thyroid function tests and blood glucose
questions.exp: Oral isotretinoin requires monitoring of fasting serum lipids (can cause hypertriglyceridemia, increasing pancreatitis risk) and liver function tests (hepatotoxicity) before starting and at 4–8-week intervals. It is a potent teratogen requiring pregnancy tests in women of childbearing potential.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man with chronic HCV infection presents with small vessel vasculitis, purpuric lesions on the legs, and arthralgia. Complement C4 is low. A cold precipitation test of serum is positive. Immunoglobulin testing shows IgM–IgG complexes. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Mixed cryoglobulinaemia type II (polyclonal IgG + monoclonal IgM rheumatoid factor) is strongly associated with chronic HCV infection. It presents as palpable purpura (leukocytoclastic vasculitis), arthralgia, and hypocomplementaemia (low C4). Cryoprecipitate forms at <37°C and redissolves on warming.

questions.q: In Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS), what makes it superior to wide local excision for recurrent basal cell carcinoma on the nose?
opts: Avoidance of general anaesthesia reducing morbidity
Real-time 100% margin examination allowing tissue-sparing clearance
Use of ionising radiation to sterilise surgical margins
Sentinel lymph node biopsy performed simultaneously
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery uses horizontal frozen sections that allow 100% peripheral and deep margin assessment in real time, ensuring complete tumour clearance while maximising tissue conservation. This is especially vital in cosmetically and functionally sensitive areas like the nose, eyelid, and ear.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with multiple warty, cauliflower-like perianal lesions. Biopsy shows koilocytes with nuclear enlargement and perinuclear halos. HPV typing reveals HPV 6 and 11. He has no evidence of malignant transformation. The most appropriate treatment?
questions.exp: Bulky/extensive condylomata acuminata (caused by HPV 6 and 11 — low-risk types) in the perianal region require surgical/laser ablation for definitive treatment. Podophyllin is contraindicated perianally and in pregnancy. Imiquimod and TCA are appropriate for smaller lesions.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with bright red, well-demarcated perianal rash with satellite pustules. The mother reports the child scratches the area frequently. KOH mount shows no fungal elements. Culture grows beta-haemolytic Streptococcus group A. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Perianal streptococcal dermatitis is caused by Group A Streptococcus (S. pyogenes). It presents in children as vivid red, well-marginated perianal erythema with intense pruritus and pain on defaecation. Negative KOH and positive streptococcal culture confirm the diagnosis. Treatment: topical or oral penicillin.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with pruritic, flesh-coloured to pink, flat-topped polygonal papules on the flexor surfaces of the wrists and ankles. Oral mucosal examination shows lacy white network on the buccal mucosa. Which cell-mediated hypersensitivity mechanism underlies this condition?
questions.exp: Lichen planus is a T-lymphocyte-mediated inflammatory dermatosis (Type IV hypersensitivity). CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells recognise altered self-antigens on basal keratinocytes, leading to vacuolar interface dermatitis and apoptosis (Civatte bodies). Wickham's striae on mucosa are pathognomonic.

questions.q: A 48-year-old male presents with a solitary, firm, skin-coloured nodule on the scalp. Histology shows sheets of tumour cells with vesicular nuclei arranged in a trabecular pattern, with positive staining for CK20 in a 'dot-like' paranuclear pattern and synaptophysin. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Merkel cell carcinoma (primary neuroendocrine carcinoma of the skin) is characterised by CK20 positivity in a perinuclear dot-like pattern and neuroendocrine markers (synaptophysin, chromogranin). Unlike metastatic SCLC (which is CK20 negative, TTF-1 positive), MCC is TTF-1 negative.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with recurrent ulcers on the oral mucosa, genital ulcers, and anterior uveitis. She also has erythema nodosum-like lesions and a positive pathergy test. Which HLA allele is most strongly associated with this condition?
questions.exp: Behçet's disease is strongly associated with HLA-B51 (subtype of HLA-B5), especially in patients from the Middle East, Turkey, and East Asia along the old 'Silk Road'. The pathergy test (sterile pustule formation 24–48h after skin prick) is positive in ~60% of cases.
